# Format: label<TAB>±other<TAB>reason. See Section 7 of the report, docs/Tinnik/REPORT.md. The routes of the paper are in docs/Tinnik/paper_routes.tsv.
# A row with the label `*` records a result used without citation throughout.

column3: Theorem 4's proof needs more than the fixed-parameter limit of Proposition 5: the estimated parameter and moving tail levels (the gap of E33). `cutTest_null` and `cutTest_alternative` prove what it needs, from the same limit theorems that prove Proposition 5, and the domination of the test distribution by Z².
Proposition 6 is the density of the test distribution, for computing p-values. The proof of Theorem 4 uses only the distribution, which `cutTail` defines directly.

The proof restricts to "generic parameters ensuring that all induced 4-networks with 4-blobs have non-cut CFs", which the paragraph before Theorem 4 takes from Theorem 1 (TINNiK's numbering), the CF-detectability of 4-blobs of Allman et al.: `External.Allman2023.cfDetectable_generic`, from lean4-allman2023's `Allman2023.cfDetectable_generic`, which passes it to the induced networks as the proof of their Corollary 1 does.

The centroid step of the paragraph before Theorem 4, on a set of four taxa with a 4-blob, uses statement (b) of the proof of Theorem 1 of Allman et al.: `External.Allman2023.isGenericNull_not_isNonCut`, from lean4-allman2023's `Allman2023.isGenericNull_not_isNonCut`.

The remaining deterministic steps of the B-quartet Inference algorithm then correctly infer all B-quartets needs that the closure under the rule (TINNiK's Theorem 2) infers only B-quartets: `External.Allman2023.closure_sound`, from lean4-allman2023's `Allman2023.closure_sound`.

The same sentence needs that the closure reaches every B-quartet (TINNiK's Theorem 3, combinatorial part): `External.Allman2023.closure_complete`, from lean4-allman2023's `Allman2023.closure_complete`.
